title: Where to Eat Near the Brandenburg Gate - Quick Summary
items: **The Brandenburg Gate sits in a food desert.** Pariser Platz, the square in front of the Gate, has only a few restaurants, all charging landmark prices for food that would embarrass a train station. The rule is simple: do not eat at the Gate, walk a few minutes first.

**For cheap and honest, walk east.** Head down Unter den Linden toward Friedrichstrasse, about ten minutes, and you reach normal Berlin streets with doner shops, bakeries and Imbiss stands where a full lunch is a few euros. A Berlin doner or a currywurst from a plain stand is the local move.

**For a proper sit-down, go into the Tiergarten or south.** Cafe am Neuen See, a lakeside beer garden about fifteen minutes west through the park, is open all year and is a real Berlin place. Or walk south to Potsdamer Platz and the Mall of Berlin for indoor food courts at everyday prices.

**The best value is a picnic.** Buy bread, cheese and fruit from a bakery or supermarket, walk two minutes west into the Tiergarten, and eat on the grass by the Neuer See. It is the cheapest good lunch near the Gate and, on a warm day, the nicest.

**Sunday changes the plan.** Shops, supermarkets and malls close on Sundays, including the Mall of Berlin food court. Buy picnic supplies at a morning bakery or the supermarkets inside Hauptbahnhof or Friedrichstrasse station, which stay open. Restaurants and beer gardens open normally.

**My free walking tour runs through this part of Mitte.** A good plan is to do the tour first, get your bearings, and then follow one of these directions to lunch afterwards, well clear of the Pariser Platz prices.
